input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new `min` parameter defaults to 1, so existing callers that did not pass `min` now get a floor of 1 second on every wait, even where the previous result was below 1 second.
- rationale: Trigger: wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1) or any configuration whose computed wait is under 1s, with min left at its default. Before this change the wait was max(0, min(result, max)), so it could be 0.1s. After it, max(max(0, 1), min(result, max)) forces at least 1s. Impact: callers who relied on sub-second backoff silently wait longer, and total retry time changes with no opt-in. The title announces a new min parameter, not a changed default, so the default-value change is not covered by it.
critique: The finding names the same defect: the new min parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0. It also gives the same failure path, where sub-second exponential results get raised to a 1-second floor, slowing retries under default options.
